Quinton Byfield won it in overtime, a snap shot at 3:37 of the extra period that ended a game LAK had controlled and then nearly handed away. Byfield, drafted second overall by the Kings in 2020 out of the Sudbury Wolves, finished with a goal and an assist. Drew Doughty set up the winner on his third assist of the night.

The Kings had led 5-1 after Artemi Panarin's power-play goal late in the second period. They had earned it: LAK out-chanced OTT 2.87 to 0.27 in expected goals (the quality of shots, not just the count) in that period alone, and finished with a 72-46 edge in shot attempts. Our deserved-to-win number, the share of simulated replays of every shot that the team wins, gave LAK 86 percent. Trevor Moore's tip-in, which started the second-period run, came on a chance worth under 1 percent. Darcy Kuemper allowed 2.3 goals more than his shots deserved.

Then OTT turned the third period into a chase. Dylan Cozens scored twice, Drake Batherson added a goal, and Shane Pinto tied it at 18:20 with the goalie pulled for an extra attacker, a tip-in on a 9 percent chance. Tim Stützle set up three goals, including both of Cozens's. OTT got there with a hit total of 37 to LAK's 27, but the Kings had the better of the play for most of the night and the winner to show for it. Both teams leave with their final scores and nothing else to report from these facts: OTT took a point from a game it trailed by four, and LAK took two from one it nearly lost.
